title: A connected positively graded algebra regular at its vertex is polynomial
statement:
Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $B$ be a finitely generated commutative unital $F$-algebra, equipped with an $\mathbf N$-grading $B=\bigoplus_{a\geq0}B_a$ by $F$-vector subspaces, with $1\in B_0$, $B_aB_b\subseteq B_{a+b}$ and $B_0=F\cdot1\cong F$. Put $\mathfrak m=\bigoplus_{a>0}B_a$, a maximal ideal with residue field $F$, and suppose the localization $B_{\mathfrak m}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]: it is Noetherian and its maximal ideal has a generating set with $\dim B_{\mathfrak m}$ elements. Here localization inverts $B\setminus\mathfrak m$, and dimension is Krull dimension. Let $b_1,\ldots,b_d\in\mathfrak m$ be any homogeneous elements whose images form an $F$-basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, where $\mathfrak m^2$ is the ideal generated by pairwise products of elements of $\mathfrak m$. Then the evaluation homomorphism
$$F[T_1,\ldots,T_d]\longrightarrow B,\qquad T_i\longmapsto b_i$$
from the polynomial algebra [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] is an isomorphism of graded $F$-algebras when $T_i$ has the strictly positive degree of $b_i$. Such a finite homogeneous basis and lifts exist, and $d=\dim_F\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2=\dim B_{\mathfrak m}$. This includes $d=0$, in which case $B=F$.

source.place: Lemma 13.39 (graded Nakayama), printed pp.268--269, and the algebra argument in Theorem 13.44, pp.271--272, with degree-zero algebra F and regularity only at the positive-degree maximal ideal. The stated local-regular variant is the agent extraction of that argument.

proof.text: The ideal $\mathfrak m^2$ is homogeneous: decompose the factors of each product into homogeneous components and collect terms of each degree. Thus $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ is positively graded. Choose finitely many algebra generators of $B$ and replace them by their finitely many homogeneous components, discarding the degree-zero components, which are scalars. These positive homogeneous elements still generate $B$ over $F$. Modulo $\mathfrak m^2$, every monomial in them of length at least two vanishes; consequently their classes span $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ over $F$. Finite linear elimination in each degree chooses a basis from these classes. The corresponding elements of $B$ are homogeneous lifts of a finite basis. In particular its size $d$ is finite; every nonzero basis class has strictly positive degree.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] to the Noetherian regular local ring $(R,\mathfrak n)$ assumed in the statement. Its residue field is $F$ by step 2. That step identifies its cotangent space with $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, so the equality clause of the cited theorem gives $\dim R=\dim_F(\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2)=\dim_F(\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2)=d$. This uses regularity only at $\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 00KU, definition-regular-local and preceding fundamental cotangent-dimension discussion.

proof.text: Now take any homogeneous lifts $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ of a basis, as in the statement, and put $C=F[b_1,\ldots,b_d]\subseteq B$. Prove $B_q\subseteq C$ by strong induction on $q\ge0$. For $q=0$ this is $B_0=F$. For $q>0$ and $x\in B_q$, the graded basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ gives $e=\sum_{\deg b_i=q}\lambda_i b_i$ with $x-e\in\mathfrak m^2$. Express $x-e$ as a finite sum of products of elements of $\mathfrak m$ and take the degree-$q$ component. This expresses it as a sum of products $uv$ with $u\in B_a$, $v\in B_b$, $a,b>0$, $a+b=q$. Both $a$ and $b$ are less than $q$, so induction puts both factors in $C$. Also $e\in C$, hence $x\in C$. Every element has a finite homogeneous decomposition, so $C=B$. By [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], evaluation defines a surjection $\phi:P=F[T_1,\ldots,T_d]\to B$, $T_i\mapsto b_i$. The same induction for an empty basis gives $B=F$ when $d=0$.

source.place: Lemma 13.39, printed pp.268--269: strong induction on positive degree, specialized to the monoid N; empty-basis case included.

proof.text: Suppose $d\ge1$ and put $I=\ker\phi$. The map $P/I\to B$, $[p]\mapsto\phi(p)$, is well defined, surjective by step 4, and injective by the definition of $I$; thus it is an $F$-algebra isomorphism, with the quotient convention [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. If $I$ contained a nonzero element, [lem-trf-polynomial-nonzero-ideal-quotient-dimension-bound], applied over the field $F$ in exactly $d\ge1$ variables, would give $\dim B=\dim(P/I)\le d-1$. On the other hand, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime] applied to the maximal (hence prime) ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $B$ gives $\dim B_{\mathfrak m}\le\dim B$: each chain counted for the localization is a chain of primes of $B$. Step 3 would then imply $d\le d-1$, a contradiction. Hence $I=0$, and $\phi$ is bijective. For $d=0$, step 4 already says $B=F$, and evaluation is the structure isomorphism $F\to B$.

source.place: Theorem 13.44, printed p.271, dimension argument following graded Nakayama; local-regular refinement using existing strict quotient-dimension and localization-chain nodes. Supporting Stacks Tags 00QK and 00E3 in the cited nodes.

proof.text: Give $T_i$ weight $\deg b_i>0$. Each monomial maps to a homogeneous element of its weighted degree, so the evaluation isomorphism preserves grading. Its inverse also preserves grading: if $x\in B_q$ and $p=\sum_a p_a$ is its preimage decomposed into weighted homogeneous parts, then $\phi(p_a)=0$ for $a\ne q$ by the direct-sum decomposition of $B$. Injectivity forces $p_a=0$ for $a\ne q$. Thus $\phi$ is an isomorphism of graded $F$-algebras. Step 1 supplies the asserted homogeneous basis and lifts, step 3 supplies the asserted dimension equality, and steps 4--5 include the zero-variable case.
